intent: Apply the Integrator's contingency for turn-response limits: narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m and reduce mass from 0.7 to 0.6 kg, keeping the validated ±0.08 m, 0.04 m-spacing, 0.016 m-footprint array, sensor y 0.05, body 0.12 x 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m fixed. Target: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.06 m with progress above 0.3, and oval finish rate at or above 55%.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Turn response is still the limit on the s-bend and slalom, so wheel_track 0.09 and mass 0.6 will raise progress and lower max_error there. (2) Counter-hypothesis: narrowing the track is overshooting on the s-bend, since s-bend progress fell from 0.177 to 0.127 when track went 0.12 to 0.10. If s-bend progress falls again or steering_oscillation rises well above 0.2 on the s-bend, the limit is overshoot and the next geometry step should be the track back to 0.10 m with a lower sensor lead or a lighter body, not further narrowing. (3) If the oval finish rate drops below 55% with line loss still at zero, return wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the shorter, lighter body. Please report per-track values, especially progress and max_error on the s-bend and slalom, and per-track steering_oscillation on the oval.
rationale: Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10, body_length 0.12, mass 0.7, with the validated ±0.08 m, 0.04 m-spacing, 0.016 m array) kept line loss at zero on every track and held rms_error at about 0.02. The oval finish rate stayed above the 55% floor at 65%, and oval steering_oscillation fell to 0.174, below the 0.25 threshold. The s-bend and slalom still ended off_track, with max_error at 0.0617 and 0.0618, at the 0.06 m floor, and progress only 0.127 and 0.093. The Integrator's stated rule matches this case: s-bend or slalom still off_track at max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.3 means turn response is still the limit, so I set wheel_track to 0.09 m and mass to 0.6 kg. The array stays fixed at ±0.08 m, so sensing is unchanged. Sensor y stays at 0.05 because oval oscillation is below 0.25. The oval finish rate is 65%, so the revert-to-0.12 m rule does not apply. There is a counter-signal I am recording rather than ignoring: s-bend progress fell from 0.177 (iteration 3, track 0.12) to 0.127 when the track narrowed. Narrowing raises the turn gain per PWM count with kp fixed, so the robot may be overshooting rather than lagging on the s-bend. The change is still the agreed next step, and the measurements requested below will show whether progress recovers. Expected result: max_error on the s-bend and slalom falls below 0.06 m, or at least progress rises above 0.13 on the s-bend. Oval finish rate holds at or above 55%.
